In this case, the wife and children are residing in the same building in the first floor which shows that they are residing in the shared household and they are kept in the same position as that of the husband.
With respect to the amount towards expenses, both the daughters have now completed degree and they cannot be considered as dependents.
Now the wife is the only dependent but as they are getting interest from the amount which is kept in deposit, in my opinion, there is no need for this court to grant any amount towards maintenance.
Further this aggrieved person is also earning which shows that they do not require any assistance from this appellant.
The property is standing in the name of the wife and in the joint name of both husband and wife.
Thus, in my opinion there is no liability on the husband to maintain the wife in this particular case because the wife is well placed compared to the husband.
24. Admittedly there are no documents produced to show that the respondent is doing any work.
His health condition is admittedly not good because only on that 27 Cr.A.25164/2014 ground he left the job and came to India.

It is the duty of the wife to take care of the husband because he is suffering from hypertension which results in anger which the wife ought to have co-operated with her husband to set right the problem.
Instead, his wife is not even inclined to talk to her husband and she is not interested to take care of him.
This is a case where this court can come to the conclusion though domestic violence is alleged by the wife and children, but it is the domestic violence caused to the husband according to me.

The allegations made against the husband are quite common things and knowing fully well that he has hypertension, the wife could have co- operated and could have sorted out things.

Though the wife has stated that he was not looking after her well, but till returning to India, I do not find any such misunderstanding as per the evidence and documents 28 Cr.A.25164/2014 available on record.
Hence, in my opinion, the Judgment passed by the trial court needs interference of this court.
Hence, I answer point No.1 in the negative and point No.2 in the affirmative.

25. Point No.3:-
 No.3:- In the result, I proceed to pass the following :
 ORDER  Appeal filed by the husband-  respondent under Section 29 of  PWDV Act
is allowed.
The petition filed by the  Petitioner-aggrieved person in  Crl.Misc.723/2010 is dismissed.
Send the LCR to the trial court  along with the copy of this Judgment.

opennyai_summary.facts:
There is no convincing evidence or materials placed by the respondent to implicate the appellant for having allegedly committed domestic violence against the respondent.
The learned trial 3 Cr.A.25164/2014 court erred in holding that the appellant is guilty of having committed domestic violence.
The amount awarded by the trial court on various heads is unjustifiable.
The trial court failed to appreciate the fact that it is not the case of the respondent that she and her daughters were depending upon the appellant for their livelihood.
The evidence of the respondent clearly shows that she had the capacity of earning.
It is contended that the appellant has no source of income and continues to be unemployed since the time he returned from Middle East in 2000.
The evidence discloses that the respondent and her daughters have been leading comfortable live.
The trial court has committed an error in not appreciating the admissions made by PW.3 that the respondent is maintaining the family from out of the fixed deposits kept in her name by the appellant.
3. The facts of the complaint are that the respondent is the husband of the aggrieved person having married on 118.1.1987 at Bangalore as per the Christian Religion rights and customs.
The aggrieved person has two female children who are majors at present.
Since last two 4 Cr.A.25164/2014 years,
the respondent is causing domestic violence and he threatened them that he will destroy the original documents of the immoveable property.
The respondent is residing separately from the aggrieved person since 19.7.2010.
The aggrieved person was earlier working in Infosys, Wipro, Phoenix Global,
NIIT, Mphasis as Communication Consultant.
The house property was purchased by her and the respondent in joint names.
She apprehends transfer of the property in the name of the respondent.
Hence, the complaint.
4. The respondent filed objections admitting the marital relationship but denied the allegation of domestic violence.
He has further contended that earlier he was living in Muscat and from 2000 he started living in Bangalore.
He has acquired the property from his hard earned money in the joint name of himself and the aggrieved person.
The aggrieved person was a housewife from 1987 to 2000 and worked only from 2000 to 2007 in Bangalore as they wanted to settle in Bangalore.
According to her throughout the marriage she suffered and the respondent traumatized her for unnecessary reasons and he had no regards for safety or health.
He habitually misconducted himself and he used to insult her.
He used to hang the pet dogs outside the bedroom window.
He locked her and her children in the house and he threatened with life.
On 25.9.2010 the respondent threatened that he would destroy the original documents of the immoveable property.
She filed complaint.
There was a cordial marital life.
He had taken care of the children as responsible parent.
As the relationship was cordial between him and his wife some of the properties were 16 Cr.A.25164/2014 registered in the name of the Petitioner and her mother on the basis of trust.
In the year 2000 they decided to quit the job and settled down at Bangalore with the family.
The Petitioner made him penniless and now he is settled down in Pune at the mercy of others.
He was always caring husband.
The Petitioner never allowed his family members either in Muscat or in Bangalore.
In the year 2010 the marital relationship became worse.
He had physical intimacy till April 2010 with the wife.
16. Their marriage was a registered marriage and thereafter it was religious marriage.
opennyai_summary.issue:
The points which arise for my consideration are:
1. Whether the trial court is justified in awarding compensation to the aggrieved person?
2. Whether the interference of this court is needed?
3. What order?
7. My answer to the above points are as follows:
 Point No.1: In the negative  Point No.2: In the affirmative  Point No.3: As per the final order  for the following:

opennyai_summary.arguments: 15. Against this, in the evidence of the respondent he had categorically stated that immediately after the marriage he went to Muscat to rejoin his employment.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Even though the ownership of the property is admitted by the respondent, he has to maintain the family by fulfilling the needs.
However, due to severe illness, the respondent was unable 22 Cr.A.25164/2014 to work for 1  years and he was doing Real Estate and social service from house itself.
However, some properties are in the joint names of himself and the aggrieved person and one property is in the name of his mother-in-law.
Now both the aggrieved person and the respondent are residing in the building purchased by them jointly.
Thus, they are staying in the shared household.
21. With respect to financial capacity, the appellant had earned money during his work at Muscat in different positions which is undisputed and also he had invested money to purchase properties in India.
She has shown ignorance that her husband had paid amount towards purchase of the property.
She has shown ignorance about the financial capacity of her mother and at that time her father was not alive.
With respect to the property situated at Hutchins road, it is undisputed that it the property purchased in the joint name.
In this case on perusal of the evidence of PW.1 to 3 it could be gathered that they have alleged that the respondent used to harass them by several modes.
Being a father, it is his responsibility to take care of the children.
Even whenever she used to come home late, her 25 Cr.A.25164/2014 father used to abuse her and it is the natural conduct of a parent.
The trial court has considered that the husband has committed domestic violence but no proper grounds are stated in the Judgment.
